questions.q: Why does WorkOrderETL.dtsx use two separate Data Flow Tasks instead of one?
options: The first task only extracts and lands raw data into staging; the second reads from staging and resolves surrogate keys before loading the warehouse — the same separation of concerns Lesson 3 argued for staging in the first place
SSIS packages are not allowed to contain more than one component per task
One Data Flow Task can only ever contain a single component
It's purely stylistic and has no effect on how the package runs
questions.explain: Splitting extraction from transformation into two tasks mirrors why staging exists at all: a bad load in one stage doesn't corrupt the other.

questions.q: What does the OLE DB Source in Data Flow Task 1 connect to, and what does its OLE DB Destination write to?
options: Source: Production.WorkOrder in AdventureWorks2012. Destination: stg.WorkOrder
Source: stg.WorkOrder. Destination: dw.FactWorkOrder
Source: dw.DimProduct. Destination: dw.FactWorkOrder
Source: Production.Product. Destination: Production.WorkOrder
questions.explain: Data Flow Task 1's entire job is landing the raw AdventureWorks2012 source table into the staging table Lesson 3 created — nothing else.

questions.q: Why is the ScrapReason Lookup in Data Flow Task 2 configured to redirect unmatched rows to a no-match output instead of failing the component?
options: A work order with nothing scrapped legitimately has no ScrapReasonID, and that has to flow through as a real NULL on ScrapReasonKey, not an error
Because ScrapReasonID is never present in Production.WorkOrder
Because the Product Lookup already handles this case
Because redirecting unmatched rows is required by every Lookup transformation by default
questions.explain: Unlike the Product lookup, a missing ScrapReasonID is expected and valid — most work orders scrap nothing, so ScrapReasonKey is nullable on the fact table by design.

questions.q: What has to already exist before Data Flow Task 2 can successfully execute?
options: dw.DimProduct, dw.DimScrapReason, and dw.FactWorkOrder — the tables the Lookups and final destination reference
Nothing — Data Flow Task 2 creates its own tables automatically
Only the Production.WorkOrder source table
Only stg.WorkOrder
questions.explain: A Lookup transformation can't resolve a key against a table that doesn't exist yet — Lesson 5 and 6 build these tables before the package can actually run end to end.
